Marketing Automation & analytics.fullContent: Here’s how you can target individuals within a buying group with personalized outreachToday’s B2B purchases rarely sit with a single decision-maker. They involve buying groups that span the entire organization. In fact, Forrester found the average buying group includes 13 stakeholders across departments and functions. And the expectations of these buying groups are only rising, with 81% of buyers wanting to form longer-term connections that transcend individual departments. Marketers are responsible for forming these lasting relationships across the entire customer lifecycle. Just as we expect for ourselves as consumers, these relationships should be personal, with each interaction building on the last.Marketers can build these connections with opportunity-based marketing (OBM), a strategy in which marketing and sales teams work together to identify, prioritize and capitalize on existing opportunities (deals in progress) and their associated buying groups, with the ultimate goal of pushing opportunities to closed-won.Opportunity-based marketing takes account-based marketing efforts a step further by narrowing in on the buying group within an account. Instead of broad, account-level messaging, you personalize at the individual level based on each buyer’s role within the buying group and broader organization (decision-maker, influencer, business user, etc). You’re also considering where they are in the sales funnel to target based on opportunity status (for example, discovery, evaluation, or negotiation).Here are a few scenarios where OBM makes sense to use:By evaluating all of your data to understand each buyer’s interests, engagement history, role, and intent, you can tailor your marketing to be more relevant to where they are in the buying cycle. A more focused strategy allows you to work more efficiently by allocating time and budget toward the opportunities most likely to close.With Agentforce Sales and Agentforce Marketing on one unified platform, you start with a connected, AI-powered system for all your customer data. This enables you to create a single view of each customer and account across sales and marketing, so you can understand how customers and key buyer personas engage with your products and content. By harmonizing data across CRM, ERP systems, data lakes and warehouses, marketing automation tools, and websites, you gain a true single view of every customer and account. You can use these insights to orchestrate more relevant, timely engagement.For example, Relationship Maps in Agentforce Sales show which stakeholders you currently know, who reports to whom, and what their sentiment is toward the brand. Relationship Maps also help you understand stakeholder roles, such as Executive Sponsor, Champion, Detractor, Decision-Maker, and more.Using shared data, sales and marketing teams can both view customer engagement, AI-driven propensity-to-buy scores, and buyer group heatmaps in the same dashboard. Marketing Automation & analytics.summary: AI agents can help marketers move faster and deepen customer relationships during the holidays. By leveraging AI, campaigns can be executed faster with personalized content, targeted recovery messages for abandoned carts, proactive order tracking updates, and instant customer support, ultimately improving customer experience and reducing support team overload.
Marketing Automation & analytics.fullContent: AI agents can help you move faster and reach customers in deeper waysThe holidays are a marketer’s dream — hello, increased engagement! — and also the biggest opportunity to build lasting customer relationships. In order to be successful, you need to execute campaigns across every channel that drive sales. But the real challenge is the need to move faster, to personalize even deeper and to connect with customers in more meaningful ways. The good news is AI agents can help you scale your efforts without exhausting your team or losing the human touch. Agentforce Marketing unlocks a new way of working where agents handle the manual tasks and you can focus on what you are best at: strategy and creativity. Here’s a breakdown of four ways agents can solve common holiday marketing headaches.The problem: Holiday planning is overwhelming. Marketers spend too much time guessing which messages will resonate and manually segmenting audiences, leading to wasted spend and irrelevant content.The solution: With AI you can accelerate campaign creation, refine audience segments and deploy high-performing content faster than ever before (hours, not weeks).The data generated by your customers’ interactions with your brand is pure gold for marketers. When you use AI to analyze this data, you gain deep, actionable insight into real customer needs and pain points, allowing you to build smarter campaigns and personalize at a depth your competitors can’t match.Best practices and tips:The problem: A customer fills their cart with gifts, gets distracted and leaves before checking out. That’s lost revenue, and it happens more often during the busy holidays.The solution: You can win back that revenue by using real-time targeting to create a highly personalized, sequenced recovery campaign across multiple channels.This isn’t just about sending a generic “Did you forget something?” message. It’s about using your data to understand the shopper’s intent and sending a perfectly timed message on the channel they check most, with the ability to offer instant, frictionless support if they have a final question.Best practices and tips:The problem: “Where’s my order?” is the most frequent question during the holiday rush. Order delays and logistical issues lead to frustrated customers and an overwhelmed support team.The solution: Proactively send real-time order tracking updates to keep customers informed across their preferred channels, dramatically reducing inbound service requests.You don’t want your customers’ first interaction with your service team to be an angry call asking where their package is. By using automated alerts, you eliminate the friction and turn a necessary transactional message into a positive engagement opportunity, backed by instant help if a real problem arises.Best practices and tips:The Problem: Holiday shoppers expect instant, reliable support.
